WHAT CHANGED:

- PagedListState gains loadMoreError (null unless the latest failure was a next page). The hook keeps it through a later background refetch, so the notice is not relabelled while that refetch runs. `error` keeps its old meaning (parked OnlinePaymentHistory relies on it).

- LoadMore: on a failed page shows an error Alert (role=alert) 'More <noun> could not be loaded, so this list is not complete.' above the same button, which now reads 'Try again' (button keeps its tree position, so focus is kept). Session-ended errors show no alert. Applies to all 36 LoadMore lists (plan said 34; Phase I added NomineeRequestQueueScreen and ClientNomineeRequestPanel).

- AsyncBoundary: when error is set and data is shown (and the error is not a page error or a session end), a warning Alert (role=status) 'The last refresh failed, so this may be out of date.' sits above the kept data, with 'Try again' (loading while refetching); no retry for forbidden/notConfigured, as ErrorState. Optional AsyncQuery.loadMoreError lets paged queries suppress it for page failures.

- loadAll queries: refetchOnMount/WindowFocus/Reconnect return false while the query is awaiting a page retry (status error + fetchMeta forward), so a stopped walk is not restarted by focus, reconnect or another screen mounting it; only the user's Try again (refetch) resumes it. Non-loadAll lists keep refreshing loaded pages on focus (the client bell shares the notifications key); those refreshes never request the failed page.

WHAT CHANGED:

- paged.ts: the page hold is a module store (WeakMap keyed by the cached Query object, plus a listener set read through useSyncExternalStore). Every hook sharing the query key sees it. It is set when a next-page fetch settles as an error (forward fetchMeta), released when a next page succeeds or when the hook's refetch is called (the error panel's / stale notice's Try again). It lives exactly as long as the query's cache entry (gcTime after the last observer, or queryClient.clear at session end); a browser reload starts clean.

- While held: the loadAll walk does not step; loadAll observers skip refetch on mount/focus/reconnect; a stopped walk keeps data undefined and returns the held error even after another hook's successful refetch cleared query.error; loadMoreError = held error for every observer, including a freshly mounted one (F1).

- AsyncBoundary: stale notice now shows when error !== loadMoreError (was: loadMoreError == null). Same for non-paged queries; for paged ones a later refresh failure (a different error object) still shows its notice beside a held page failure.

- LoadMore: remembers its button when pressed while focused; when isLoadingMore ends and focus is on body/null, focuses the button again (still connected only). Covers both a failed and a successful Show more. The Alert text is wrapped in a span with useId and the button gets aria-describedby while failed. No button at all for AUTHORIZATION_DENIED (errorVariantOf === forbidden); the alert and 'N so far' stay.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE vs 9ba2251 (deliberate): after a failed Show more, a later successful background refetch no longer clears the 'not complete' alert; it stays with 'Try again' until the user retries (runtime report item 5 will now read differently). A write that invalidates a held loadAll list refreshes loaded pages but keeps the error panel until Try again.

TEST (rule 10): paged.test.ts 'does not re-request a failed page after another hook sharing the query refreshes it': loadAll hook fails page 2, unmounts; a non-loadAll hook on the same key refetches page 1 (asserted: 2 first-page reads) and still reports the failure as loadMoreError (F1); the loadAll hook remounts: failed page requested once only, data undefined, error = failure; refetch (Try again) then loads both pages.
